div.l: Eủerich a word yf it be in his charge
Al speke he neủer so rudely ⁊and large
Or elles he mot telle his tale vn trewe
Or feyne thinges or fynde wordys newe
He may nought spare al thogh he were his brother
He mote also wel seiȝe o word as an other
Crist spak him self ful brode in holy writte
And wel ȝe woot ne velenye is itte
Ek Plato seith ho so can hym rede
The wordis mote be Cosyn to þe dede
Also y preye yow for yiue it me
All haue I not sett folk in her degre
Here in þis tale as þat þei shuld stonde
My wit is short ye may wel vnderstonde
Greet chere maad oure ost vs ev̉erychon
And to þe soper sette he vs a noon
He suede vs wit vitailles at þe beste
Strong was the wyn and wel drinke vs leste
A semely man oure oost was wit alle
For to ben a marchall in an halle
A large man he was wit eieȝen stepe
A Fairer burgeis is noon in chepe
Bold of his speche ⁊and wys ⁊and wel y taught
And of Manhod him lakkede right nouht
Eke þ̉er to he was ryght a mery man
And aft̉er soper pleyȝen he bigan
And spak of merþe among oþ̉ere þinges
Whan that we hadde made our rekenynges
And seide þus . Now lordynges trewely
Ye ben to me welcome right hertely
For bi my trouthen yf þat I schal not lye
I sey noght this yeer so mery a companye
At oones in this herberwe as is now
Fayn wolde I don yow merthe wiste I how
And of a merthe I.am ryght now bi þought
To don yow ese ⁊and it schal coste nought
Ye gon to Canturbery god yow spede
Þe blisseful martir quyte ȝow ȝoure mede
And wel y woot as ȝe gon by þe weye
Ye shapyn yow to talen ⁊and to pleye
For trewely confort ne merthe is noo
